issues.legal_issue: Limitation for a suit to set aside an instrument begins when the plaintiff learns the facts entitling them to challenge it, and knowledge of the instrument’s contents is not established merely because a relative signed as an identifying witness after being misled about its nature.
material_facts: The plaintiffs filed a suit to challenge a purported sale deed and recover possession, asserting that they learned of it after an inquiry prompted by the failure to provide them their share of the properties’ produce.

A son of the executant had signed as an identifying witness at registration, but the appellate court accepted that he had been told the document concerned management of the properties and did not know its contents.
The appellate court found that the plaintiffs learned of the sale deed around 6 June 1966 and filed suit on 11 July 1966.
The Supreme Court found no sufficient reason to interfere with the concurrent findings that the suit was not barred by limitation.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not barred by limitation because it was filed within the applicable period after the plaintiffs learned the facts entitling them to challenge the deed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 59 of the Limitation Act, 1963, time runs from when the facts entitling a plaintiff to have an instrument cancelled or set aside become known. The court accepted the finding that the identifying witness had been misled about the document’s nature; signing as an identifying witness did not, in these circumstances, establish knowledge of its contents. The Supreme Court declined to disturb the appellate court’s factual finding on knowledge.

predicates.instrument_cancellation_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking to cancel or set aside an instrument.
predicates.plaintiff_learned_challenge_facts_after_: The plaintiff learned the facts underlying the challenge after the instrument was executed.
predicates.identifying_witness_unaware_of_instrumen: A person who identified the executant at registration did so without knowing the instrument’s contents.
predicates.suit_filed_within_limit_from_knowledge: The plaintiff filed suit within the applicable limitation period after learning the facts underlying the challenge.

issues.definition: If a plaintiff brings an instrument-cancellation suit, learns the facts underlying the challenge after execution or an identifying witness lacked knowledge of the contents, and files within the applicable period after learning those facts, the suit is not barred by limitation.

issues.legal_issue: When a challenged instrument is nominal and unsupported by consideration, a possession decree following its invalidation must reflect the interest the transferor actually held in each property.
material_facts: The purported sale deed was found to be nominal and unsupported by consideration, and the claim of an earlier oral relinquishment and the claim of title by adverse possession were rejected.
The schedule showed that the deceased held the whole of the properties in items I and II, while he held a one-sixth share in the properties identified in the operative decree as items III and VI.

The appellate decree awarded possession of the whole of items I to III and a one-sixth share in item IV; the Supreme Court modified the decree to award possession of items I and II and a one-sixth share in items III and VI.
issues.conclusion: The deed was declared null and void, and the plaintiffs and supporting defendants were entitled to possession of the whole of items I and II and a one-sixth share in items III and VI.
issues.legal_principle: The court treated the nominal deed without consideration as conferring no title and tailored possession relief to the deceased’s established ownership interest in each property. It relied on the property descriptions in the deed and plaint schedule and on the concurrent findings rejecting the alleged oral relinquishment and adverse possession.

predicates.instrument_cancellation_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking to cancel or set aside an instrument and recover possession.
predicates.instrument_found_nominal_without_conside: The court found that the instrument was nominal and that no consideration supported it.
predicates.transferor_owned_entire_property: The evidence established that the transferor owned the entire property purportedly conveyed.
predicates.transferor_owned_fractional_property: The evidence established that the transferor owned only a fractional interest in the property purportedly conveyed.

issues.definition: When an instrument-cancellation suit concerns a nominal instrument without consideration, the possession decree is limited to the transferor’s established interest, whether that interest is the whole property or only a fraction.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff who succeeds in a suit for possession may receive mesne profits from the filing of the suit when no mesne profits for an earlier period were claimed.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought possession of the properties but did not claim mesne profits for a period before filing suit.
An interim order had directed ascertainment of profits, and the court stated that the plaintiffs could receive a decree for mesne profits upon payment of the appropriate stamp.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs were entitled to mesne profits from the date the suit was filed, subject to payment of the appropriate stamp.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit seeking possession, the successful plaintiffs were entitled to mesne profits from the filing of the suit where they had not sought mesne profits for an earlier period; the court had directed ascertainment of profits and made the decree subject to payment of the appropriate stamp.

predicates.possession_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking possession of property.
predicates.plaintiff_entitled_to_possession: The court determined that the plaintiff was entitled to possession of the property.
predicates.no_pre_suit_mesne_profits_claimed: The plaintiff did not claim mesne profits for a period before filing the suit.

issues.definition: If a plaintiff succeeds in a possession suit and did not claim mesne profits for an earlier period, mesne profits are awarded from the filing of the suit.
